QUAD 44 · PREAMPLIFIER

Restoring your Quad 44

The Quad 44 is a preamplifier made from 1979 to 1989. It chooses your source and sets volume and tone. It replaced the Quad 33. Each input is a small plug-in module, so different 44s can have different inputs.

This guide is new. Nobody has checked its parts list against a real Quad 44 yet, so treat it as a starting point.

Before anything else: stay safe

This preamplifier plugs into the mains. Parts inside can still give you a dangerous shock after it is unplugged.

If you are new to electronics, don't open it. You can do everything on this page from the outside. A qualified technician does the work inside.

Four steps

1

Write down a few details

You can find all of these from the outside.

  • The serial number. It decides which of DADA's three kits you need.
  • The finish: brown (early) or grey (later).
  • Which input modules are fitted, and your turntable cartridge if you use one.
  • Any faults: inputs changing on their own, clicks, a chattering relay at switch-on, or a thump at switch-off.
2

Talk it through with an AI assistant

An AI assistant with the Quad Agent guide checks your details against Quad's own documents and tells you what applies to your Quad 44. It asks questions first and never guesses part values.

Copy this into your AI assistant:

Read quad-upgrade/SKILL.md and follow it to help me restore my Quad 44. Start by helping me identify it from the outside.

It needs the guide files first. Download the guide and add it to your assistant, or give it the quad-upgrade folder.

3

Choose what you want done

The recap

A recap replaces the ageing capacitors, the chips that do the amplifying and the chips that switch the inputs. It includes Quad's own fix for inputs that change by themselves.

Optional extras

These change how the Quad 44 behaves. You don't need any of them.

  • Lower noise on the radio and aux inputs. Removes resistors that 1970s chips needed and modern ones don't.
  • Quieter at volume zero. For early models that are not fully silent with the volume turned right down.
  • Relay fix. Only needed if the relay chatters when you switch on.
4

Take it to a technician

Send them the link to this page. Everything they need is in the section below: the parts list, Quad's service documents and the upgrade guides.

Ask them to check the parts against your actual Quad 44 before ordering. Quad changed things during production, and earlier owners may have too.

Good to know

  • Moving coil and other unusual input modules need a special kit from DADA.
  • Many of the 44's capacitors have no + or − marking on the board. Your technician must note each one before taking it out.
  • If the inputs jump around by themselves, Quad published a fix. It is part of the recap.
